services.name: Spotify
services.description: Lists Spotify playlists, liked tracks, albums, and artists into /v1/library/*. Full playlist items via content transport /v1/services/spotify/playlists/{id}/items.

services.name: YouTube Music
services.description: Lists YouTube Music playlists and liked videos into /v1/library/*. Playlist items via content transport. Shares the Google connection.

services.name: Amazon Music
services.description: Lists Amazon Music playlists into /v1/library/playlists. Full playlist items via content transport.

services.name: Tidal
services.description: Tidal access is not permitted in this environment

services.name: Google Photos
services.description: Google Photos via the Picker API: the user selects photos once; Aegis lists that selection as neutral metadata. Photo bytes stay on Google Photos (non-Aegis canonical). Shares the Google connection with YouTube and Contacts.

services.name: Immich
services.description: Self-hosted Immich photo library. Photo bytes stay on Immich (foreign/local canonical). Set canonical_for: ["photos"] here if Immich is your home copy (and remove it from google-photos).

services.name: Google Contacts
services.description: Lists Google People/Contacts address-book entries as neutral contacts so photo.people[] and other types can share identity matching. Shares the Google connection.

services.name: Google Calendar
services.description: Lists Google Calendar events as neutral calendar entries so /v1/library/events can answer schedule questions. Event content stays on Google Calendar (non-Aegis canonical). Shares the Google connection.

services.name: Gmail
services.description: Lists Gmail messages as neutral message metadata so /v1/library/messages can answer email questions. Message bodies stay on Gmail (non-Aegis canonical). Shares the Google connection.

services.name: YNAB
services.description: Live YNAB budget transactions for /v1/library/transactions. Prefer a Personal Access Token in headers (Aegis owns the secret). Amounts map from milliunits to signed decimal strings.

services.name: Quicken
services.description: Locally imported Quicken QIF/QFX files. Import with -import-quicken or POST /v1/services/quicken/import. Line-item metadata only — statements/PDFs are never stored.

services.name: Bluesky
services.description: Share photos to Bluesky as public image posts (ownership-claim PoC, issue #20). Aegis stores no photo bytes; it fetches from the canonical photo service, posts a copy, and returns a sha256 + post_uri claim. Image embeds cap at 1MB. Use an app password, not your main password.

services.name: Paperless-ngx
services.description: Self-hosted Paperless-ngx documents (receipts, warranties, leases, letters). File bytes stay on Paperless (foreign/local canonical). Set canonical_for: ["documents"] here if Paperless is your home copy. Use documents=metadata to list titles/tags without text.

services.name: Google Drive
services.description: Google Docs via Drive for /v1/library/documents. Content is HTML/plain-text export (markdown conversion deferred). Files stay on Drive (non-Aegis canonical). Shares the Google connection; drive.readonly covers list + export. Watch OAuth app verification limits (same class as Photos).

services.name: DAV Contacts
services.description: CardDAV address book (Nextcloud, iCloud, Fastmail, Radicale, Baïkal). Lists contacts as neutral Contact values. Credentials are username + app-specific password (never echoed by admin/API). Set canonical_for: ["contacts"] if this DAV server is your home copy (and remove it from Google Contacts).

services.name: DAV Calendar
services.description: CalDAV calendar (Nextcloud, iCloud, Fastmail, Radicale, Baïkal). Lists events as neutral CalendarEvent values with RRULE expansion in the requested window. Credentials are username + app-specific password. Set canonical_for: ["events"] if this DAV server is your home copy (and remove it from Google Calendar). Events also feed /v1/library/freebusy.

services.name: GitHub
services.description: GitHub contacts for /v1/library/contacts — organization members and followed users as neutral Contact values (name, email, handle, company). Profile metadata only; no repos, issues, or activity. Shares the GitHub OAuth connection (read:user, read:org).
